reference.title: Scenario 10: 2-column table in an API reference section

section.p: Consider a Markdown table that contains parameters for alarm configuration.

entry.codeblock: ### Alarm Configuration Parameters | Parameter | Default Value | Description | |-----------|---------------|-------------| | Enabled | True | Enables alarm generation | | Severity | Medium | Alarm severity level | | Auto Clear | False | Clears alarms automatically |

<reference id="alarm_configuration_parameters"> <title>Alarm Configuration Parameters</title> <refbody> <properties> <prophead> <proptypehd>Parameter</proptypehd> <propvaluehd>Default Value</propvaluehd> <propdeschd>Description</propdeschd> </prophead> <property> <proptype>Enabled</proptype> <propvalue>True</propvalue> <propdesc>Enables alarm generation</propdesc> </property> <property> <proptype>Severity</proptype> <propvalue>Medium</propvalue> <propdesc>Alarm severity level</propdesc> </property> <property> <proptype>Auto Clear</proptype> <propvalue>False</propvalue> <propdesc>Clears alarms automatically</propdesc> </property> </properties> </refbody> </reference>

section.p: Result:The converter recognizes the table as a parameter-definition table because the first column contains parameter names and the remaining columns describe parameter attributes. Instead of generating a generic DITA table, the converter creates a DITA reference topic containing a <properties> element. The heading immediately preceding the table becomes the topic title, and each table row is converted into a <property> entry.
section.note: Use a consistent parameter table structure with columns such as Parameter , Default Value , Description , Type , or Required . Consistent column naming improves the converter's ability to identify parameter-definition tables and generate DITA reference structures instead of generic tables.
